title: Python & numerical ML
subtitle: Programming fluency, data, matrices and your first model
deliverable: A reproducible NumPy training script, predictions, loss plot and short README.
tasks: Generate a synthetic dataset with fixed random seed
Implement vectorized predictions, MSE and gradients
Train weights with gradient descent and chart the loss
Evaluate on held-out samples and document findings

days.title: Python environment & reproducibility
days.explanation: A virtual environment isolates packages; a fixed random seed makes stochastic demonstrations easier to reproduce.
days.practice: Create a venv, print Python and NumPy versions, and sample five seeded random numbers.
days.quiz: What does a virtual environment isolate?
days.explanationAnswer: Project dependencies. A virtual environment isolates packages; a fixed random seed makes stochastic demonstrations easier to reproduce.

days.title: Functions, iteration & clean scripts
days.explanation: Small reusable functions help separate data generation, predictions and evaluation; iterations process batches predictably.
days.practice: Implement make_data(n, seed) and calculate sample means in a reusable function.
days.quiz: Why use a function for data generation?
options: It makes experiments reusable and testable
days.explanationAnswer: It makes experiments reusable and testable. Small reusable functions help separate data generation, predictions and evaluation; iterations process batches predictably.

days.title: NumPy arrays & shapes
days.explanation: An array shape describes its axes; for example (32, 10) represents 32 samples with 10 features each.
days.practice: Build arrays of shapes (3,), (2,3), and (4,2,3), then print their dimensions.
days.quiz: What does shape (32,10) often represent?
days.explanationAnswer: 32 samples with 10 features. An array shape describes its axes; for example (32, 10) represents 32 samples with 10 features each.

days.title: Broadcasting & vectorization
days.explanation: Broadcasting aligns compatible dimensions; vectorization performs bulk operations without Python loops over every element.
days.practice: Normalize a 2x3 array by subtracting a three-value mean vector.
days.quiz: For shape (2,3) minus (3,), what is the result shape?
days.explanationAnswer: (2,3). Broadcasting aligns compatible dimensions; vectorization performs bulk operations without Python loops over every element.

days.title: Dot products & matrices
days.explanation: Matrix multiplication combines compatible inner dimensions and creates the outer-dimension result, a key neural-network operation.
days.practice: Multiply a (4,3) feature matrix by a (3,1) weight matrix.
days.explanationAnswer: (4,1). Matrix multiplication combines compatible inner dimensions and creates the outer-dimension result, a key neural-network operation.

days.title: Prediction, error & dataset splits
days.explanation: The model predicts targets; a loss measures error. A held-out test set checks generalization rather than memorization.
days.practice: Create y=2x+1 with noise, split samples, and implement mean squared error.
days.quiz: Why keep a held-out test set?
options: To remove the need for metrics
days.explanationAnswer: To measure generalization. The model predicts targets; a loss measures error. A held-out test set checks generalization rather than memorization.

days.title: Week 1 project: gradient descent
days.explanation: Gradient descent adjusts parameters opposite their loss gradients; changing the learning rate affects convergence.
days.practice: Train slope and bias using NumPy, and visualize loss for different learning rates.
days.quiz: What does a gradient identify?
days.explanationAnswer: How loss changes with parameters. Gradient descent adjusts parameters opposite their loss gradients; changing the learning rate affects convergence.

title: PyTorch & neural networks
subtitle: Autograd, nonlinear layers, optimization and validation
deliverable: A CPU-ready PyTorch MLP with a saved state_dict and train/test metrics.
tasks: Generate nonlinear binary-classification data
Build a 2-layer MLP with nn.Module or nn.Sequential
Train with autograd and an optimizer; plot training loss
Evaluate on a distinct test set and reload checkpoint

days.title: PyTorch tensor basics
days.explanation: PyTorch tensors extend numerical arrays with device placement and automatic differentiation features.
days.practice: Create float32 tensors, reshape a batch, and compare with NumPy values.
days.quiz: What does a tensor's dtype control?
days.explanationAnswer: Its numeric representation. PyTorch tensors extend numerical arrays with device placement and automatic differentiation features.

days.title: Derivatives & sensitivity
days.explanation: A derivative is local sensitivity. For squared error (w-2)^2, the gradient is 2(w-2).
days.practice: Differentiate a quadratic by hand and verify with finite differences.
days.quiz: At w=0 for (w-2)^2, what is the derivative?
days.explanationAnswer: -4. A derivative is local sensitivity. For squared error (w-2)^2, the gradient is 2(w-2).

days.title: Chain rule through a graph
days.explanation: The chain rule connects derivatives through composed operations such as weight → prediction → error → loss.
days.practice: Draw a graph of yhat=wx and L=(yhat-y)^2, then derive dL/dw.
days.quiz: Why is the chain rule important?
options: It propagates gradients through composed functions
days.explanationAnswer: It propagates gradients through composed functions. The chain rule connects derivatives through composed operations such as weight → prediction → error → loss.

days.title: Automatic differentiation
days.explanation: Autograd records differentiable operations and computes gradients for tensors marked requires_grad.
days.practice: Compute a scalar loss, call backward(), inspect gradients, then clear them.
days.quiz: What does loss.backward() calculate?
options: Gradients of loss with respect to trainable inputs
days.explanationAnswer: Gradients of loss with respect to trainable inputs. Autograd records differentiable operations and computes gradients for tensors marked requires_grad.

days.title: Neurons, activation & MLPs
days.explanation: Linear layers alone compose into a linear map; nonlinear activations let networks model nonlinear boundaries.
days.practice: Build a 2→16→1 PyTorch network with Tanh or ReLU.
days.quiz: Why insert an activation between linear layers?
options: To make input tensors always one-dimensional
days.explanationAnswer: To model nonlinear relationships. Linear layers alone compose into a linear map; nonlinear activations let networks model nonlinear boundaries.

days.title: SGD, Adam & learning rates
days.explanation: Optimizers apply gradient-informed updates; too-large step sizes can oscillate or diverge.
days.practice: Compare SGD training at three learning rates and record the loss curves.
days.quiz: What can an excessively large learning rate cause?
days.explanationAnswer: Divergence or oscillation. Optimizers apply gradient-informed updates; too-large step sizes can oscillate or diverge.

days.title: Week 2 project: MLP classification
days.explanation: A complete training pipeline uses train/test splits, a loss function, an optimizer and checkpointing.
days.practice: Train a binary classifier on two-feature nonlinear samples and save its state_dict.
days.quiz: What is a logit in binary classification?
days.explanationAnswer: An unnormalized prediction score. A complete training pipeline uses train/test splits, a loss function, an optimizer and checkpointing.

title: Tokenization & embeddings
subtitle: Text becomes token IDs, vectors and attention scores
deliverable: A notebook that tokenizes text, produces embedding tensors and explains token-shape changes.
tasks: Compare at least two tokenization strategies
Inspect input IDs, attention masks and padding behavior
Create toy embedding lookup examples with shapes
Explain and visualize a tiny attention-softmax example

days.title: Language modeling objectives
days.explanation: Autoregressive models estimate the next token conditional on previous tokens, rather than storing a simple question-answer table.
days.practice: Create a small token sequence and construct shifted input and target IDs.
days.quiz: For a causal LM, what is a training target?
options: The next token at each position
days.explanationAnswer: The next token at each position. Autoregressive models estimate the next token conditional on previous tokens, rather than storing a simple question-answer table.

days.title: Tokenizers and IDs
days.explanation: Tokenizers map text to discrete token IDs. A token is not necessarily a word or a character.
days.practice: Tokenize the same text with a pretrained tokenizer and compare the decoded output.
days.quiz: Do tokenizers always produce one token per word?
options: They do not use numerical IDs
No; words may split into subword tokens
days.explanationAnswer: No; words may split into subword tokens. Tokenizers map text to discrete token IDs. A token is not necessarily a word or a character.

days.title: Subword tokenization intuition
days.explanation: BPE-like tokenization combines frequent pieces into reusable subword units, balancing vocabulary size and sequence length.
days.practice: Count repeated character pairs in a toy corpus and simulate one merge step.
days.quiz: Why use subwords instead of only full words?
options: They can represent uncommon words using shared pieces
days.explanationAnswer: They can represent uncommon words using shared pieces. BPE-like tokenization combines frequent pieces into reusable subword units, balancing vocabulary size and sequence length.

days.title: Embedding lookup
days.explanation: An embedding table maps token IDs into learned dense vectors that models can operate on.
days.practice: Create an nn.Embedding(100,8), pass token IDs, and inspect the output shape.
days.quiz: For input IDs of shape (2,4) with width 8, output shape is?
days.explanationAnswer: (2,4,8). An embedding table maps token IDs into learned dense vectors that models can operate on.

days.title: Position information
days.explanation: Transformers need a mechanism to represent token order because attention by itself does not enforce sequence position.
days.practice: Add toy position vectors to token embeddings and compare two reordered sequences.
days.quiz: Why are position signals useful?
options: They set the model's learning rate
They reduce sequence length to one
days.explanationAnswer: They help represent token order. Transformers need a mechanism to represent token order because attention by itself does not enforce sequence position.

days.title: Scaled dot-product attention
days.explanation: Attention uses query-key similarity, a softmax over scores, and weighted sums of value vectors.
days.practice: Calculate a 2-token attention matrix and check row-wise softmax sums.
days.quiz: What should each attention-softmax row sum to?
days.explanationAnswer: Approximately 1. Attention uses query-key similarity, a softmax over scores, and weighted sums of value vectors.

days.title: Week 3 project: tokenizer explorer
days.explanation: Link text, token IDs, embedding shapes and attention weights into a coherent pipeline.
days.practice: Build a token/embedding notebook and explain shape transformations for each stage.
days.quiz: What is the primary input to an embedding lookup?
days.explanationAnswer: Integer token IDs. Link text, token IDs, embedding shapes and attention weights into a coherent pipeline.

title: Transformer inference
subtitle: Masks, decoder blocks, sampling, caching and model loading
deliverable: A runnable inference notebook with prompt controls, seed logging and latency comparisons.
tasks: Draw and explain a minimal decoder transformer block
Implement toy scaled dot-product attention with causal mask
Run a small pretrained model with its tokenizer
Compare two decoding strategies and log latency

days.title: Multi-head attention
days.explanation: Multiple attention heads learn different projections, which are concatenated and projected back into the model dimension.
days.practice: Sketch two heads and verify projected dimensions when splitting the model width.
days.quiz: What is one purpose of multiple attention heads?
options: To train one unrelated model per word
days.explanationAnswer: Different learned attention projections. Multiple attention heads learn different projections, which are concatenated and projected back into the model dimension.

days.title: Causal masking
days.explanation: A causal mask prevents a next-token decoder from attending to tokens that come after the current position.
days.practice: Create a 4x4 lower-triangular attention-visibility mask.
days.quiz: In causal self-attention, a token can see:
days.explanationAnswer: Earlier tokens and itself. A causal mask prevents a next-token decoder from attending to tokens that come after the current position.

days.title: Transformer block anatomy
days.explanation: A decoder block typically contains attention, feed-forward layers, normalization and residual connections.
days.practice: Draw a block diagram with residual paths and track its tensor shapes.
days.quiz: What do residual connections primarily provide?
options: A path that helps information and gradients flow
days.explanationAnswer: A path that helps information and gradients flow. A decoder block typically contains attention, feed-forward layers, normalization and residual connections.

days.title: Logits, softmax & sampling
days.explanation: Logits are converted to probabilities; temperature adjusts the distribution, and decoding chooses tokens.
days.practice: Compare greedy decoding and temperature-adjusted sampling from example logits.
days.quiz: What does lower temperature often do?
days.explanationAnswer: Sharpen the next-token distribution. Logits are converted to probabilities; temperature adjusts the distribution, and decoding chooses tokens.

days.title: KV cache & inference latency
days.explanation: A KV cache reuses earlier attention key/value computations during autoregressive generation, trading memory for faster token generation.
days.practice: Draw prefill vs decode phases and list what each phase computes.
days.quiz: Why use a KV cache?
options: Retrain the transformer at every token
Avoid recomputing past keys and values
days.explanationAnswer: Avoid recomputing past keys and values. A KV cache reuses earlier attention key/value computations during autoregressive generation, trading memory for faster token generation.

days.title: Loading pretrained models
days.explanation: Loading a model and its matching tokenizer allows reproducible inference with a specified checkpoint and configuration.
days.practice: Run a small pretrained model locally and record prompt, decoding config and latency.
days.quiz: Why pin the model revision?
options: To reproduce the same checkpoint and tokenizer
days.explanationAnswer: To reproduce the same checkpoint and tokenizer. Loading a model and its matching tokenizer allows reproducible inference with a specified checkpoint and configuration.

days.title: Week 4 project: inference comparison
days.explanation: A careful inference comparison controls model, prompts, seeds and decoding settings.
days.practice: Compare two decoding settings on fixed prompts and report latency and outputs.
days.quiz: What is a fair comparison strategy?
options: Change prompts and model at the same time
days.explanationAnswer: Hold unrelated experimental conditions constant. A careful inference comparison controls model, prompts, seeds and decoding settings.

title: Fine-tuning & LoRA
subtitle: Dataset hygiene, SFT objectives and parameter-efficient updates
deliverable: A tiny supervised dataset, LoRA training run, adapter artifact and baseline comparison.
tasks: Create and validate a small instruction/response dataset
Record baseline predictions and task metrics
Train a PEFT LoRA adapter on a suitably small open-weight model
Evaluate held-out performance and save adapter + metadata

days.title: Instruction dataset format
days.explanation: Supervised fine-tuning requires consistent prompt, response and masking conventions compatible with the chosen trainer.
days.practice: Design a small JSONL instruction dataset and validate fields.
days.quiz: Why is a consistent dataset schema valuable?
options: It prevents preprocessing and supervision mismatches
days.explanationAnswer: It prevents preprocessing and supervision mismatches. Supervised fine-tuning requires consistent prompt, response and masking conventions compatible with the chosen trainer.

days.title: Cleaning and deduplication
days.explanation: Duplicates, malformed records and contamination bias both training and evaluation.
days.practice: Write validators for empty responses, duplicate prompts and non-UTF8 data issues.
days.quiz: Why deduplicate before fine-tuning?
options: To reduce redundant examples and leakage risks
days.explanationAnswer: To reduce redundant examples and leakage risks. Duplicates, malformed records and contamination bias both training and evaluation.

days.title: Splits & leakage prevention
days.explanation: Evaluation examples must not leak into training, even through paraphrases or shared source documents.
days.practice: Split your data by source group and check for near-duplicate overlap.
days.quiz: What is data leakage?
options: When evaluation information enters model training or selection
days.explanationAnswer: When evaluation information enters model training or selection. Evaluation examples must not leak into training, even through paraphrases or shared source documents.

days.title: SFT objectives and masking
days.explanation: Supervised fine-tuning often optimizes token prediction on desired response segments with an appropriate training mask.
days.practice: Inspect an instruction/response batch and identify which tokens contribute to loss.
days.quiz: Why might prompt tokens be masked in SFT?
options: To focus loss on desired response tokens
To reduce all gradients to zero
days.explanationAnswer: To focus loss on desired response tokens. Supervised fine-tuning often optimizes token prediction on desired response segments with an appropriate training mask.

days.title: LoRA: low-rank updates
days.explanation: LoRA represents a trainable weight update with two small matrices while holding base weights fixed.
days.practice: Calculate full-matrix vs rank-4 adapter parameter counts.
days.quiz: What is normally frozen in LoRA?
days.explanationAnswer: The pretrained base weights. LoRA represents a trainable weight update with two small matrices while holding base weights fixed.

days.title: Selecting LoRA configuration
days.explanation: Adapter rank, alpha, dropout and target modules affect capacity, compute and which layers can adapt.
days.practice: Compare trainable parameter counts for ranks 4, 8 and 16.
days.quiz: What does adapter rank change?
options: The update's capacity and parameter count
days.explanationAnswer: The update's capacity and parameter count. Adapter rank, alpha, dropout and target modules affect capacity, compute and which layers can adapt.

days.title: Week 5 project: train an adapter
days.explanation: A clean LoRA experiment saves the adapter plus its base-model reference and configuration.
days.practice: Train a small LoRA adapter with a tiny dataset and compare held-out metrics.
days.quiz: What is usually smaller to save with LoRA?
options: The original dataset as GPU memory
days.explanationAnswer: The adapter checkpoint. A clean LoRA experiment saves the adapter plus its base-model reference and configuration.

title: QLoRA & evaluation
subtitle: Memory budgets, checkpoints, tests and reproducibility
deliverable: A controlled experiment report comparing a baseline and efficient adaptation method.
tasks: Estimate model-memory footprints and practical VRAM limits
Prepare model + training checkpoints and repeatable config
Run a small, feasible fine-tuning experiment or documented simulation
Report task quality, retention, latency and GPU-hour estimates

days.title: Quantization and bit width
days.explanation: Quantization stores approximate parameter values in lower-precision representations, reducing model memory at possible accuracy cost.
days.practice: Estimate raw parameter memory for FP16, INT8 and 4-bit formats.
days.quiz: What happens to raw weight storage at 4 bits vs 16 bits?
days.explanationAnswer: About one-quarter, ignoring overhead. Quantization stores approximate parameter values in lower-precision representations, reducing model memory at possible accuracy cost.

days.title: QLoRA design
days.explanation: QLoRA combines a quantized frozen backbone with trainable low-rank adapters, often allowing adaptation with less VRAM.
days.practice: Draw the memory layout of base weights, adapters, optimizer states and activations.
days.quiz: Which parts are generally trained in QLoRA?
days.explanationAnswer: The added adapter parameters. QLoRA combines a quantized frozen backbone with trainable low-rank adapters, often allowing adaptation with less VRAM.

days.title: Gradient accumulation & checkpointing
days.explanation: Accumulation approximates a larger effective batch through multiple microbatches; activation checkpointing trades recomputation for memory.
days.practice: Compute effective batch size and configure a tiny accumulation loop.
days.quiz: If microbatch=2 and accumulation=8, effective batch per worker is?
days.explanationAnswer: 16. Accumulation approximates a larger effective batch through multiple microbatches; activation checkpointing trades recomputation for memory.

days.title: Model checkpoints & metadata
days.explanation: A trustworthy checkpoint ties weights or adapters to base revision, tokenizer, dataset, config, and evaluation procedure.
days.practice: Create an experiment manifest with exact revisions, seed and training settings.
days.quiz: Why store a tokenizer revision with a checkpoint?
options: To remove the need for datasets
Token mappings and preprocessing must match
days.explanationAnswer: Token mappings and preprocessing must match. A trustworthy checkpoint ties weights or adapters to base revision, tokenizer, dataset, config, and evaluation procedure.

days.title: Quality, retention & cost metrics
days.explanation: A model upgrade needs old-task retention, new-task performance, inference costs and repeatability—not just one accuracy score.
days.practice: Design a result table comparing two methods across five metrics.
days.quiz: What best detects catastrophic forgetting?
options: Old-task scores before and after an update
days.explanationAnswer: Old-task scores before and after an update. A model upgrade needs old-task retention, new-task performance, inference costs and repeatability—not just one accuracy score.

days.title: Ablations & controlled experiments
days.explanation: An ablation changes one experimental factor at a time so observed effects are interpretable.
days.practice: Vary only adapter rank and hold data, seed and training steps constant.
days.quiz: What is the point of an ablation?
options: Isolate the effect of one design decision
days.explanationAnswer: Isolate the effect of one design decision. An ablation changes one experimental factor at a time so observed effects are interpretable.

days.title: Week 6 project: efficient update benchmark
days.explanation: Comparing methods requires identical held-out tests and accounting for memory, time and quality.
days.practice: Create an efficiency and retention report with clear limitations.
days.quiz: Which metric alone is insufficient?
days.explanationAnswer: Training loss. Comparing methods requires identical held-out tests and accounting for memory, time and quality.

title: Continual learning
subtitle: Model drift, catastrophic forgetting and old/new evaluation
deliverable: A two-stage task experiment reporting new-task gain, old-task retention and forgetting.
tasks: Define clearly separated old-task and new-task evaluations
Measure untouched baseline on both tasks
Update a small model and re-evaluate all task groups
Compare against a rehearsal or replay baseline and analyze regressions

days.title: Knowledge drift
days.explanation: A model's knowledge can become stale when facts or task distributions change, even if stable capabilities remain useful.
days.practice: Create dated evaluation questions and classify them as stable vs time-sensitive.
days.quiz: What can drift monitoring reveal?
options: The true age of every fact
days.explanationAnswer: Changing performance on current tasks. A model's knowledge can become stale when facts or task distributions change, even if stable capabilities remain useful.

days.title: Catastrophic forgetting
days.explanation: Training on new tasks can reduce performance on older tasks as weight updates interfere with prior knowledge.
days.practice: Train sequentially on two toy tasks and measure old-task accuracy after each stage.
days.quiz: What is catastrophic forgetting?
options: Old-task performance declining after learning new tasks
days.explanationAnswer: Old-task performance declining after learning new tasks. Training on new tasks can reduce performance on older tasks as weight updates interfere with prior knowledge.

days.title: Rehearsal and replay
days.explanation: Replay interleaves a limited sample of older examples during new-task training to mitigate forgetting.
days.practice: Reserve a small replay buffer and compare outcomes with and without replay.
days.quiz: What does replay add to later training?
days.explanationAnswer: Selected historical examples. Replay interleaves a limited sample of older examples during new-task training to mitigate forgetting.

days.title: Regularization-based retention
days.explanation: Methods such as EWC discourage large changes to parameters judged important for earlier tasks, with assumptions and trade-offs.
days.practice: Describe an importance-weighted penalty and compare it to replay conceptually.
days.quiz: What does EWC try to protect?
days.explanationAnswer: Parameters important for old tasks. Methods such as EWC discourage large changes to parameters judged important for earlier tasks, with assumptions and trade-offs.

days.title: Adapters and task routing
days.explanation: Separate adapters can isolate updates, but a routing decision is needed to choose which capability to apply.
days.practice: Design rules to select among task-specific adapters and identify ambiguous cases.
days.quiz: What challenge comes with multiple adapters?
options: Choosing the correct adapter for a task
days.explanationAnswer: Choosing the correct adapter for a task. Separate adapters can isolate updates, but a routing decision is needed to choose which capability to apply.

days.title: Old/new evaluation protocol
days.explanation: Before an update, freeze independent old/new test sets and record baselines; after an update, report both scores.
days.practice: Compute retention and new-task gain from a synthetic before/after table.
days.quiz: Why use the same held-out tests before and after?
days.explanationAnswer: To measure comparable changes. Before an update, freeze independent old/new test sets and record baselines; after an update, report both scores.

days.title: Week 7 project: forgetting benchmark
days.explanation: Reliable continual-learning claims require baseline, updated, and retention-preserving comparison conditions.
days.practice: Run a two-stage toy benchmark and report per-task results and limitations.
days.quiz: What is the strongest evidence of retention?
options: Stable held-out old-task performance after updating
A lower new-task training loss alone
days.explanationAnswer: Stable held-out old-task performance after updating. Reliable continual-learning claims require baseline, updated, and retention-preserving comparison conditions.

title: AI lifecycle observatory
subtitle: Experiment tracking, model registry, metrics and upgrade decisions
deliverable: A working evaluation dashboard with versioned runs, comparisons and retain/upgrade/replace recommendations.
tasks: Define model, dataset, run and metric entities
Persist experimental metrics and checkpoint references
Build charts for quality, forgetting, latency and costs
Document your decision rules and audit one model lifecycle

days.title: Experiment run tracking
days.explanation: Each run should capture inputs, code revision, settings, metrics, and artifacts to enable meaningful comparisons.
days.practice: Create JSON run manifests and a local run table for three experiments.
days.quiz: What is an experiment run ID used for?
options: Linking a configuration to its metrics and artifacts
days.explanationAnswer: Linking a configuration to its metrics and artifacts. Each run should capture inputs, code revision, settings, metrics, and artifacts to enable meaningful comparisons.

days.title: Model registry & lineage
days.explanation: A registry links deployed versions to checkpoints, dependencies and evaluation approvals.
days.practice: Design model-version and parent-checkpoint records with lifecycle status.
days.quiz: What does lineage answer?
options: Which source data and checkpoints produced a version
How many CPUs are installed globally
days.explanationAnswer: Which source data and checkpoints produced a version. A registry links deployed versions to checkpoints, dependencies and evaluation approvals.

days.title: GPU-hours & quality economics
days.explanation: Compute budgets require separating training cost from ongoing inference, maintenance, and storage.
days.practice: Estimate GPU-hours = devices × runtime hours and compare two upgrade methods.
days.quiz: If 2 GPUs each run for 3 hours, how many GPU-hours?
days.explanationAnswer: 6. Compute budgets require separating training cost from ongoing inference, maintenance, and storage.

days.title: Dataset versioning
days.explanation: Versioned datasets and immutable splits keep experiments comparable as training content changes.
days.practice: Create dataset version IDs, SHA-256 hashes and evaluation-set policies.
days.quiz: Why pin a test-set revision?
options: To compare models against the same questions
To force the model to remember facts
days.explanationAnswer: To compare models against the same questions. Versioned datasets and immutable splits keep experiments comparable as training content changes.

days.title: Benchmark dashboards
days.explanation: A dashboard should show actual observed metrics and make baselines, uncertainty and regressions visible.
days.practice: Plot old/new accuracy and total cost for versioned runs; label all demo numbers.
days.quiz: Which dashboard choice is misleading?
options: Mixing illustrative and actual numbers without labels
days.explanationAnswer: Mixing illustrative and actual numbers without labels. A dashboard should show actual observed metrics and make baselines, uncertainty and regressions visible.

days.title: Lifecycle decision rules
days.explanation: Upgrade, retain, specialize, archive, or replace should follow explicit performance and total-cost thresholds.
days.practice: Write a rule-based selector for a model that fails new-data benchmarks.
days.quiz: What should guide a replacement decision?
options: Quality, constraints and total lifecycle cost
days.explanationAnswer: Quality, constraints and total lifecycle cost. Upgrade, retain, specialize, archive, or replace should follow explicit performance and total-cost thresholds.

days.title: Week 8 project: observatory dashboard
days.explanation: A useful observatory links data lineage, experiment evidence, costs and an explainable recommendation.
days.practice: Implement an experiment registry UI and compare model-update strategies.
days.quiz: What makes a dashboard recommendation auditable?
options: An explanation tied to recorded metrics and rules
days.explanationAnswer: An explanation tied to recorded metrics and rules. A useful observatory links data lineage, experiment evidence, costs and an explainable recommendation.

title: Independent research capstone
subtitle: Design an original model-longevity experiment and publish a repeatable report
deliverable: A self-contained research report with datasets, configs, figures, limitations and repeatability instructions.
tasks: Write a falsifiable model-longevity hypothesis and evaluation protocol
Freeze the data splits and baseline configuration
Run at least two upgrade strategies under documented constraints
Write results, caveats, costs and next-research questions

days.title: Write a falsifiable hypothesis
days.explanation: A research hypothesis makes a measurable prediction that an experiment could disprove.
days.practice: Define a quality-retention-cost hypothesis and criteria for rejecting it.
days.quiz: What makes a hypothesis falsifiable?
options: Evidence could show it is wrong
days.explanationAnswer: Evidence could show it is wrong. A research hypothesis makes a measurable prediction that an experiment could disprove.

days.title: Design evaluation datasets
days.explanation: Use independent datasets with dated facts, stable knowledge and general reasoning tests; remove contamination.
days.practice: Freeze data splits, labels and scoring scripts, and document provenance.
days.quiz: What should never be tuned on repeatedly?
days.explanationAnswer: A final held-out test set. Use independent datasets with dated facts, stable knowledge and general reasoning tests; remove contamination.

days.title: Freeze baseline & budgets
days.explanation: Measure unchanged models before intervention and define equal budgets and acceptable regression thresholds.
days.practice: Record baseline metrics and compute budget in an immutable manifest.
days.quiz: Why measure the baseline first?
options: To quantify whether an intervention improves outcomes
days.explanationAnswer: To quantify whether an intervention improves outcomes. Measure unchanged models before intervention and define equal budgets and acceptable regression thresholds.

days.title: Execute two upgrade strategies
days.explanation: Hold evaluation constant while comparing methods such as RAG, LoRA or continued training.
days.practice: Run two feasible interventions with logged configs and failure handling.
days.quiz: What is necessary for a valid method comparison?
days.explanationAnswer: Same independent evaluation protocol. Hold evaluation constant while comparing methods such as RAG, LoRA or continued training.

days.title: Analyze forgetting and uncertainty
days.explanation: Report per-task changes, error types and variance across seeds if possible; distinguish illustrative from measured values.
days.practice: Create result charts and discuss uncertainty, limitations and alternative explanations.
days.quiz: Why report task-level scores?
days.explanationAnswer: Aggregates can hide important regressions. Report per-task changes, error types and variance across seeds if possible; distinguish illustrative from measured values.

days.title: Publish a reproducible report
days.explanation: A credible research artifact includes code, environment, datasets, exact configs and limitations.
days.practice: Prepare README, scripts, evaluation tables and an explicit reproducibility checklist.
days.quiz: What belongs in a reproducible report?
options: Only a screenshot of a chart
Configs, data provenance, metrics and limitations
days.explanationAnswer: Configs, data provenance, metrics and limitations. A credible research artifact includes code, environment, datasets, exact configs and limitations.

days.title: Week 9 capstone: model longevity
days.explanation: Turn measurements into a defensible decision about upgrade versus replacement under defined constraints.
days.practice: Present a mini-paper and identify one next experiment capable of changing your conclusion.
days.quiz: What would justify choosing an older upgraded model?
options: Meeting quality and cost constraints on independent evaluation
